# Explanation Consistency of ML-Based IoT Intrusion Detection

This repository contains the code used for *Explaining the Black Box: An XAI-Driven Trustworthiness Audit of ML-Based IoT Intrusion Detection Across Attack Categories*.

The public reproduction package contains three files: `primary_reproduction.ipynb`, `README.md`, and `requirements.txt`. Pre-generated result files are not distributed. The notebook creates its own results directory when it runs.

## Running the analysis

1. Use Python 3.12.13.
2. Download the CICIoT2023 CSV release from the Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity at `https://www.unb.ca/cic/datasets/iotdataset-2023.html`, then place all 169 CSV files directly inside `data/`.
3. Install the pinned dependencies with `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt`.
4. Open `primary_reproduction.ipynb` and run all cells from a clean kernel.

The notebook checks the expected file count, working-set size, feature count, primary model configuration, and the main manuscript values. It stops with an explicit error if required inputs are missing or if a validation check falls outside its stated tolerance.

A full run is computationally intensive. The Random Forest SHAP calculation, XGBoost searches, LIME explanations, bootstrap analysis, permutation analysis, and counterfactual generation account for most of the runtime.

## Data preparation

The notebook samples up to 2,000 rows from each distributed CSV file and caps each original attack label at 50,000 rows. It produces a 336,004-row working dataset, uses a stratified 70/30 train/test split with base seed 42, removes `LLC`, removes six features that are constant in the training partition, and retains 39 modelling features.

The cap changes the raw CICIoT2023 distribution. Class proportions reported by the notebook refer to the capped working dataset.

The 169 distributed CSV files are mixed Spark-style partitions rather than capture-session groups. The notebook also reports exact and rounded-vector overlap across the train/test boundary. These diagnostics do not exclude dependence among correlated nonidentical flows.

## Model selection

Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression use balanced class weighting during cross-validation and final fitting. XGBoost uses balanced sample weights computed separately within each training fold. The primary XGBoost configuration is `learning_rate = 0.3`, `max_depth = 6`, and `n_estimators = 200`.

The `learning_rate = 0.1`, `max_depth = 6`, `n_estimators = 200` model is retained only as a comparison configuration for the protocol-sensitivity analysis.

## Generated outputs

The notebook writes generated tables, figures, diagnostics, model objects, and validation files to `results/`. These files are outputs of the run and are not part of the public repository package.

The final validation cell compares the main reproduced values with the manuscript using the stated tolerances. DiCE uses genetic search and can return different counterfactual solutions across runs. Its aggregate proximity and sparsity values can vary slightly even when the same software versions and seeds are used.


## Manuscript output mapping

The notebook writes all generated files to `results/`. The main manuscript objects map to the following outputs:

| Manuscript object | Generated output |
| --- | --- |
| Table XI, aggregate performance | `table_aggregate_performance.csv` |
| Table XII, per-category F1 and initialisation stability | `table_per_category_f1.csv`, `table_initialisation_stability.csv` |
| Table XIV, ECS sensitivity | `table_ecs_sensitivity.csv` |
| Table XV, chance baseline and adjusted/permutation ECS | `ecs_chance_baseline.csv`, `ecs_adjusted.csv`, `ecs_global_permutation.csv` |
| Table XVI, bootstrap and category stability | `table_ecs_bootstrap_and_reduced.csv`, `table_category_stability_summary.csv` |
| Table XVII, XGBoost protocol comparison | `sensitivity_aggregate.csv`, `sensitivity_per_category_f1.csv`, `sensitivity_ecs.csv` |
| Table XVIII, Spearman analysis | `table_spearman.csv` |
| Table XIX, matched LIME/SHAP analysis | `lime_levels_by_category.csv`, `lime_levels_overall.csv` |
| Table XX, category SHAP profiles | `per_category_top_features.csv` |
| Table XXI, counterfactual analysis | `counterfactuals.csv`, `counterfactual_top_changed_features.csv` |
| Figure 1 | `figures/manuscript_fig1_f1_heatmap.png` |
| Figure 2 | `figures/manuscript_fig2_shap_per_category.png` |
| Figure 3 | `figures/manuscript_fig3_ecs_sensitivity.png` |
| Figure 4 | `figures/manuscript_fig4_ecs_heatmaps.png` |
| Figure 5 | `figures/manuscript_fig5_ecs_f1_scatter.png` |
| Figure 6 | `figures/manuscript_fig6_confusion_matrix.png` |

Additional diagnostic CSV files are also generated by the notebook. They are outputs of the run rather than files distributed with the public repository.
